case.case_title: Seetha Weerakoon v. Mahendra, O.I.C. Police Station, Galagedera and Others

clause.text: No person shall be arrested except according to law and must be informed of the reason.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was lawfully arrested and informed of the reason for her arrest as required by Article 13(1) of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed that she was arrested without valid grounds, was not informed of the reason for her arrest, and was detained unlawfully without proper detention orders.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents argued that the petitioner was arrested under valid detention orders issued under the Emergency Regulations and that the detention was lawful pending investigations into subversive activities.
key_facts: Petitioner was arrested on 12 August 1989 and detained at Galagedera Police Station.
Detention orders under Emergency Regulations were issued but expired or were not continuous.
Petitioner was not informed of the specific reason for her arrest.
Advisory Committee was unaware of the reason for detention.
No material was produced to justify the arrest or detention.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that Article 13(1) requires that a person arrested must be informed of the reason for the arrest. A mere reference to a regulation without specifying the offence is insufficient. The State must provide material to justify the arrest to enable objective determination of its reasonableness.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The petitioner was not informed of the specific reason for her arrest, and the Advisory Committee itself was unaware of the grounds for detention. The respondents failed to produce any material evidence to justify the arrest, rendering it unlawful under Article 13(1).
principles_established: Arrest must be according to law and the arrested person must be informed of the reason.
A bare statement or reference to a regulation is insufficient to satisfy Article 13(1).
The State must produce material evidence to justify the arrest.
precedents_cited: Nanayakkara v. Henry Perera [1985] 2 Sri LR 375

outcome.holding: The court held that the arrest of the petitioner was unlawful and violative of Article 13(1) as she was not informed of the reason for her arrest and no valid grounds were shown.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The petitioner was awarded compensation and the detention order was quashed.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(1) is central to the court's reasoning as the petitioner’s fundamental right to be informed of the reason for arrest was violated, which led to the finding of unlawful arrest and detention.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The Advisory Committee itself had not been aware of the reason for her arrest, supporting her complaint that she was not informed of the reason for her arrest as required by Article 13(1). No material has been placed before Court to justify the arrest.
